_: Every hotspot family the house can build into. THE ONLY HAND-MADE FILE IN THE FURNITURE
PIPELINE - tools/genfurn.py turns it into the enum tables, the varps, the constants and all of
poh_furniture.rs2.
key      the ^poh_fam_<key> constant, and the order families are numbered in. NEVER REORDER:
the family number is not stored, but the ITEM number is, and item numbers follow
family order. Append only.
label    what the Furniture creation menu puts in its title bar
room     which room the hotspots are in, for the docs and for battery check 28
hotspots hotspot loc ids, checked against the six template squares
shape    the locshape every piece of this family is placed with - it has to be the shape its
hotspot carries in the template, or loc_add lands on a different layer and the
hotspot is not replaced
locs     the buildable locs, in tier order. Each must carry op5=Remove in poh.loc.
planks   how many planks a piece costs, the same at every tier, as OSRS mostly does
base     the family's base Construction level; a tier costs base + 7 per wood step + 3 per
tier within that wood
NOT WIRED, and why: rugs, curtains, windows, floor decor and the combat ring are multi-tile
assemblies of 6 to 19 hotspots that per-piece storage is the wrong shape for; the portal chamber
needs a frame-then-destination flow of its own; the garden's centrepiece is where the exit portal
stands; wall decorations and mounted shields are 48 locs each and need a menu that pages by
material first; and the costume room's storage units have no locs in the 474 import.

op1.line: A larder, and it never runs out.
Crockery, and there is always more of it.

op1.mes: You sit down on the bench.

lines: Nobody comes. You have not hired a servant yet.
There is still plenty of the day left for building.
There is nothing here but books you have already read.

op1.mes: You look at yourself. Your reflection looks back, unimpressed.

op1.line: The tools are all where you left them.

op1.mes: You play a tune. It sounds rather nice.

lines: You gaze at the stars. You feel very small.
You look through the telescope. A shooting star crosses the sky.
You watch the clouds drift past. Nothing much is happening up there.
You peer through the telescope and see the moon, very close up.

op1.mes: You sit on your throne and survey your kingdom.
You sit down on the bench.

lines: The crawling hand waves a finger at you.
The cockatrice head fixes you with a stony look.
The basilisk head stares blankly past your shoulder.
The kurask head says nothing. It never did have much to say.
The abyssal demon head whispers something you would rather not have heard.
The dragon heads snap at each other, then at you.
The kalphite queen's head clicks its mandibles.
A rack for the gloves you would box in.
There are no boxing gloves in this world to hang on it.

families.label: Rug space
families.room: parlour, bedroom, skill hall, quest hall, chapel

shape_allowances.why: The parlour has three Chair spaces and two of them are centrepiece_diagonal while the third is centrepiece_straight. A family carries one shape, and storing a second would change the packed record every save already holds. Both shapes are LocLayer.GROUND (engine routefinder/flags.ts), so loc_add still REPLACES the hotspot rather than standing beside it - the only difference is that the chair in those two corners renders square to the room instead of at 45 degrees.

labels._: Per-loc label overrides. Two reasons a loc is on this list: a cache name that does not fit the Furniture creation window's 126px name column, and a cache name that is not the thing's real name - all seven lecterns come out of the 474 import called just 'Lectern', when they are the oak / eagle / demon / teak / mahogany ladder OSRS names and the models plainly show it. The two mahogany ones lose the word 'lectern' because the full name is 135px; genfurn.py measures every label in the client's own font and refuses to emit one that overflows, which is why this list is short and exact.

cameras._: Per-family camera for the Furniture creation window's model icon, as [xan, yan]. The default is ^poh_menu_xan/^poh_menu_yan - three quarters on, from slightly above - which is right for anything with depth. A framed picture has none: seen from three quarters it is a one-pixel sliver. These families are turned face-on instead. Kitchen shelves and tool racks are walldecor too and are NOT in this list, because they do have depth and the default suits them.

_ops: op1 is what the piece does when it is left-clicked. Every family that has one carries it at op1 -
checked - so the trigger is always [oploc1,<loc>] and tools/genfurn.py writes one per piece into
poh_furn_ops.rs2.
sit      play a seq and say something. 377 has no seated state, so this is the emote and not
a pose you hold.
light    needs a tinderbox; swaps the loc for its lit twin and REMEMBERS it (bit 22 of the
packed record, which reads as 0 in every save written before this round)
altar    pray at it to restore prayer points; use anything with a bone_exp param on it to
offer the bones for boosted experience
jingle   play a midi
observe  one of several lines at random
talk     one line per tier, in tier order
preen    a seq and a line
mes      lines, printed in order
study    open the lectern window (tools/gentablets.py) and make magic tablets
search   open the Search window (tools/genpohsearch.py) on the piece's own list of items, one
tier at a time. The contents are unlimited - every wiki page for these says so - so
the window is a picker and not a store: taking one adds to the player and the grid
does not change. `tiers` is one list per loc IN LOC ORDER, so the mapping from the
wiki's tiers to this cache's is positional, which matters because the names differ
(this repo's Oak shelves 1 is the wiki's Wooden shelves 3) and the levels do too.
NOT ANSWERED YET, and why: Work-at (workbenches) is flatpacks and needs one obj per piece of
furniture; Craft, Open, Change-clothes, Upgrade, Activate, Set-up, Shoot-at, Throw-at,
Challenge-mode, Pull, Use and Make-helmet all need either new objects, a new interface, or a
servant. Rub on the mounted Amulet of Glory wants the glory teleport, which lives inside a
label that also eats a charge - it has to be pulled out into a proc first.

poh_exit_portal is the level-1 Centrepiece of BOTH the garden and the formal garden, which is
what OSRS does - so a formal garden is also somewhere a way out can be built. The two
centrepiece lists have nothing else in common.
